Rashi on Nazir 21b:11:1.english: Rather, it is obvious that the husband nullified [it] for her - And [the Mishnah] teaches that she incurs the forty [lashes] for having drunk wine and contracted ritual impurity from the dead before he nullified [it] for her.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:12:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך מיעקר עקר לה בעל - והכא במאי עסקינן דסופגת את הארבעים? כגון דלא היפר לה. ודקאמרת: "אי לא היפר לה בעל, צריכא למימר?" — ודאי לא צריכא, אלא משום דקתני סיפא כו':
Rashi on Nazir 21b:12:1.english: Actually, I could say to you: The husband uproots [it] for her - And with what are we dealing here, where she incurs the forty [lashes]? For instance, where he did not nullify [it] for her. And as for what you said: "If the husband did not nullify [it] for her, does it need to be said?" — certainly it does not need [to be said], but rather because the latter clause teaches, etc.:

Rashi on Nazir 21b:12:2.hebrew: אינה סופגת - דצריכא למימר, דס"ד דתספוג, כיון דנתכוונה לאיסורא:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:12:2.english: She does not incur [lashes] - For it needed to be stated, as it could enter your mind [to say] that she should incur [them], since she intended [to commit] a forbidden act.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:1:1.hebrew: ורמינהו כו' זה הכלל כו' - ופה ושיער לא הוי דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו, דאי גייז לשיער וחתיך לניב שפתים — לא מיית:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:1:1.english: And they raised a contradiction, etc., This is the principle, etc. - And the mouth and hair are not an entity upon which life depends, for if one shears the hair and severs the lips, he does not die.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב יהודה דאמר הכי יעשה פי כפיו מיין - דהואיל דפריש הכי, הוי נזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:2:1.english: Rav Yehuda said that he said like this: Let my mouth be like his mouth from wine - For since he specified thus, he is a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:3:1.hebrew: אמרה הריני נזירה ושמע בעלה ואמר ואני שניהם נזירין ואינו יכול להפר לה - דכיון דאמר ואני, גלי אדעתיה דניחא ליה במאי דקא נדרה איהי, והשתא מקיים לה:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:3:1.english: [If] she said, “I am hereby a nazirite,” and her husband heard and said, “And I,” both of them are nazirites, and he cannot nullify [it] for her - For since he said, “And I,” he revealed his intention that he is pleased with what she vowed, and he has now confirmed [it] for her.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת מיעקר עקר - בעל את הנדר מעיקרו, אישתכח דבההיא שעתא דקאמרה חבירתה ״ואני״, דלא חייל עלה נזירות כלל:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:1.english: And if you say [that he] uproots [it] - [That the] husband [uproots] the vow from its inception, it turns out that at that time when her companion said "And I," naziriteship did not take effect upon her at all.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:2.hebrew: ואי אמרת מיגז גייז - דמכאן ולהבא לא חייל עלה נזירות, אבל למפרע הוות נזירה:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:2.english: And if you say he severs [it] - That from this point forward, the naziriteship does not take effect upon her, but retroactively she was a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:3.hebrew: איהי אישתראי וחבירתה אסירא - דלכי אמרה "ואני", הוות חבירתה נזירה מעליא:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:4:3.english: She is released and her companion is bound - For when she [the second woman] said "And I," her companion [the first woman] was a full-fledged nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:5:1.hebrew: ואי ס"ד בעל מיגז גייז - את הנדר מכאן ולהבא, אמאי אינו יכול להפר משום דקאמר "ואני"? נימא דהאי דאמר "ואני" — להכי הוא דקאמר הכי: דתהוי נזירה לפי שעה עד דליקבל עליה נזירות, וליגזייה לנזירות אשתו מכאן ולהבא, ונזירות דידיה תיחול עליה כדמעיקרא, דהא אינו מיפר מכאן ולמפרע:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:5:1.english: And if it should enter your mind that the husband severs - [Namely,] the vow from that moment onward — why is he unable to nullify [it merely] because he said, "And I"? Let us say that this [statement] that he said, "And I," it was for this [purpose] that he said it: that she should be a nazirite temporarily until he accepts naziriteship upon himself; and let him [then] sever his wife’s naziriteship from that moment onward, and his own naziriteship will take effect upon him as from the outset, since he does not nullify retroactively.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:5:2.hebrew: אלא לאו שמע מינה - הבעל, כי מיפר לנזירות אשתו, מיעקר עקר לה, ומשום הכי אינו יכול להפר לה — שאם יהא מיפר לה, נמצא מיפר את שלו, דמיעקר עקר. והיינו טעמא דאינו יכול להפר את שלה: משום דבההיא שעתא דאמר ״ואני״, ניחא ליה דתהוי נזירה עד דחייל עליה נזירות, דהא קיים לה לפי שעה; ומההיא שעתא ואילך לא מצי מיפר, משום דבעל מיעקר עקר, דלעולם אינו יכול להפר מכאן ולהבא בלא מפרע, והכא למפרע לא מצי מיפר, דהא קיים לה לפי שעה:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:5:2.english: Rather, must one not conclude from it - When the husband nullifies his wife's naziriteship, he uproots it [entirely], and for this reason he cannot nullify [it] for her — for if he were to nullify [it] for her, he would turn out to nullify his own [vow], since he uproots [it entirely]. And this is the reason that he cannot nullify hers: because at that time when he said, "And I," he was pleased that she be a nazirite until the naziriteship took effect upon him, as he upheld [it] for her temporarily; and from that time onward he cannot nullify [it], because a husband uproots [the vow], for he can never nullify from this point forward without [doing so] retroactively, and here he cannot nullify retroactively, as he upheld [it] for her temporarily.

Rashi on Nazir 21b:6:1.hebrew: לא לעולם מיגז גייז - אלא היינו טעמא דלא מצי מיפר לה: דכיון דאמר לה "ואני", כמ"ד לה "קיים נזירותיך" דמי. והלכך, אי מיתשיל אהקמתו — אהא דקא מקיים לה ברישא — מצי מיפר, ואי לא — לא מצי מיפר:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:6:1.english: No; actually, he severs - Rather, this is the reason that he cannot nullify [it] for her: since he said to her, "And I," he is considered like one who says to her, "Your naziriteship is upheld." And therefore, if he seeks dissolution of his upholding — of that which he upheld for her initially — he can nullify [it]; and if not, he cannot nullify [it].

Rashi on Nazir 21b:7:1.hebrew: ואם שלה היתה הבהמה - וכגון שהקנה לה אחר לנזירותה, ואמר לה: על מנת שאין לבעליך רשות בה:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:7:1.english: And if the animal was hers - And [this is], for example, where another [person] transferred ownership [of it] to her for her naziriteship, and said to her: "On the condition that your husband has no rights in it."

Rashi on Nazir 21b:9:1.hebrew: והיינו טעמא - דתמות, דכיון שהפרישה לשם חטאת מעיקרא, והשתא לא מצטרכה לכפרה — דהא היפר לה בעלה ועקר את הנדר מעיקרו — הויא לה כחטאת שמתו בעליה, דגמירי דלמיתה אזלא, לפי שאין כפרה למתים. ואית דמפרשי: כיון דצריכה כפרה על שציערה עצמה מן היין, והשתא לא צריכה, דהיפר לה בעלה מעיקרא — הויא לה כחטאת שמתו בעליה, דגמירי דלמיתה אזלא; דאפילו ר"א הקפר מודה דלא קרבה אפי' על הצער, משום דהויא לה כחטאת שמתו בעליה — משום דבחטאת בהמה גמרינן דתמות, אבל בחטאת העוף לא גמרינן דתמות:
Rashi on Nazir 21b:9:1.english: And this is the reason - That it must die: For since she designated it as a sin-offering originally, and now she does not require atonement — since her husband nullified [the vow] for her and uprooted the vow from its inception — it is [treated] as a sin-offering whose owner died, about which it is learned [by tradition] that it goes to death, because there is no atonement for the dead. And some explain: Since [initially] she required atonement for having distressed herself [by abstaining] from wine, and now she does not require [it], because her husband nullified [it] for her from the outset — it is [treated] as a sin-offering whose owner died, about which it is learned [by tradition] that it goes to death; for even Rabbi Eleazar HaKappar concedes that it is not sacrificed even for the distress, because it is [treated] as a sin-offering whose owner died — because regarding an animal sin-offering we learn [by tradition] that it must die, but regarding a bird sin-offering we do not learn that it must die.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:10:1.hebrew: היכי דמי אילימא דלא היפר לה בעל - כלל — צריכא למימר דלוקה? דהא נזירה היא, ופשיטה הוא דלוקה! אלא פשיטא: דהיפר לה הבעל אחר שנטמאה ואחר ששתתה, ואפילו הכי לוקה — דבההיא שעתא דשתתה ביין הוי נזירה, וש"מ: הבעל מיגז גייז:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:10:1.english: What are the circumstances? If we say that the husband did not nullify [her vow] - [Meaning,] at all — need it be said that she incurs lashes? For she is indeed a nazirite, and it is obvious that she incurs lashes! Rather, it is obvious that the husband nullified [the vow] for her after she became defiled and after she drank, and even so she incurs lashes — for at that time when she drank wine she was a nazirite; and deduce from this: the husband severs [the vow].

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:12:1.hebrew: לעולם מיעקר עקר - ומיירי שלא היפר. ודקאמרת: "צריכא למימר?", משום סיפא, דאיצטריך ליה למיתני "אינה סופגת", תני רישא אגב סיפא ד"סופגת". וסיפא איצטריכא ליה למיתני לאפוקי מדרבי יהודה, דאמר דכי נמי היפר לה בעלה ושתתה יין לוקה מכת מרדות. ואם תאמר: מאי איריא היפר לה ואחר כך היתה שותה? לאשמועינן שתתה ונטמאה, ואח"כ (שתתה) היפר לה — [דאינה] סופגת, כיון דמיעקר עקר! וי"ל: דמשום רבי יהודה נקט הכי, דאפילו בהיפר ואח"כ שתתה סופגת מכת מרדות, אע"ג דכבר היפר, כיון דלאיסורא נתכוונה:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:12:1.english: Actually, [the husband] uproots [the vow] - And [the first clause of the mishna] is dealing with [a case where the husband] did not nullify [her vow]. And as for that which you said: "Need this be said?" — because of the latter clause, where it was necessary for [the tanna] to teach "she does not incur [the forty lashes]," he taught the first clause alongside the latter clause, [saying] that "she incurs [the forty]." And the latter clause was necessary for him to teach to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yehudah, who said that even if her husband nullified [the vow] for her and she drank wine, she is flogged with lashes of rebellion. And if you say: Why specifically [did the mishna teach that] he nullified [the vow] for her and afterward she was drinking? Let it teach us [a case where] she drank and rendered herself impure, and afterward (she drank) he nullified [it] for her, [that she does not] incur [lashes], since [his nullification] uproots [the vow retrospectively]! And one can say: It formulated [the case] this way on account of Rabbi Yehudah, [to teach] that even where he nullified and afterward she drank, she incurs lashes of rebellion even though he had already nullified, since she intended [to commit] a prohibition.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:1:1.hebrew: ידי נזירה כו' - וה"ה במתניתין, אי לא "פי כפיו" אלא "פי נזיר" ו"שערי נזיר" — לא אמר כלום, דאין הנשמה תלויה בו:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:1:1.english: "My hand is a nazirite," etc. - And the same law applies to our Mishnah: if [he had] not [said] "my mouth is like his mouth," but rather "my mouth is a nazirite" and "my hair is a nazirite," he has not said anything, since life does not depend on it.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:2:1.hebrew: דאמר פי כפיו מיין - כלומר: במתניתין שאני, הואיל ושמע חבירו שנדר — ודאי קאמר הכי לענין איסור יין; אבל בברייתא, דקאמר מעצמו בלא שמיעה דחבירו נזיר — לאו כלום הוא, כיון דאין הנשמה [תלויה בו]. ופי כפיו מיין מהני אפילו לרבי שמעון, דאמר לעיל (נזיר דף ג:) "עד שיזיר מכולן" — הכא מודה דלא גרע מידות; וכן מהריני מסלסל ומכלכל דפ"ק (לעיל נזיר דף ב.) דהוי נזיר. וא"ת: כי אמר נמי "ידי נזיר", [נימא] דה"ק: "ידי כידו מלהטמאות למתים, ורגלי כרגלו מלהכנס בבית הקברות"? וי"ל: דאה"נ, דאי שמע לחבירו שנדר בנזיר ואמר "ידי כידו" — מהני; וה"נ תניא בתוספתא (פ"ג) ברישא דברייתא בהדיא: "ידי כידו, רגלי כרגלו — הרי זה נזיר":
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:2:1.english: That he said: "My mouth is like his mouth from wine" - That is to say: In the Mishnah it is different, since he heard his fellow vow, he certainly said this with regard to the prohibition of wine; but in the baraita, where he spoke on his own, without hearing that his fellow is a nazirite, it is nothing, since life [does not depend upon it]. And [saying] "My mouth is like his mouth from wine" is effective even according to Rabbi Shimon, who said above (Nazir 3b) [that one does not become a nazirite] "until he vows naziriteship from all of them" — here he concedes, as it is no worse than yadot [incomplete designations of vows]; and similarly from "I am hereby [a hair] curler" and "growing [my hair]" in the first chapter (above, Nazir 2a), which [render him] a nazirite. And if you say: When one also says "My hand is a nazirite," [let us say] that this is what he meant: "My hand is like his hand [with regard to refraining] from defiling oneself by corpses, and my foot is like his foot [with regard to refraining] from entering a cemetery"? And one can answer: That is indeed so, for if he heard his fellow who took a nazirite vow and said "My hand is like his hand," it is effective; and so too it is taught explicitly in the Tosefta (Chapter 3) in the opening clause of the baraita: "My hand is like his hand, my foot is like his foot — he is a nazirite."

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:3:1.hebrew: בעל מיעקר קא עקר - הנדר מעיקרא כשמפר לאשתו, והוי כאילו לא חל מעולם, כמו חכם שעוקר הנדר מעיקרו; או מיגז גייז — מהפרה ואילך הוא דמתבטל הנדר, ועד ההפרה היה מקויים:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:3:1.english: "Does a husband uproot" - [Does he uproot] the vow from its inception when he nullifies [it] for his wife, and it is as though it never took effect, like a Sage who uproots the vow from its root; or does he sever — [meaning that] it is from the nullification onward that the vow is canceled, and until the nullification it was in effect.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:4:1.hebrew: אי אמרינן מיעקר עקר חבירתה נמי מישתראי - שהרי הוא כאילו לא חל הנדר מעולם. ואי אמרינן מיגז גייז — היא מישתראי וחבירתה אסורה, לפי שהיתה הראשונה בכל דין נזירות עד ההפרה, ושפיר מיתפיס בה שניה, והפרת הראשונה אינה מועלת לשניה. ונהי דלגבי חכם הותר הנדר הראשון הותרו כולם, היינו משום דחכם עוקר הנדר מעיקרו, ונמצא כאילו לא חל מעולם; אבל בעל שמיפר בלא חרטה, אינו עוקר הנדר מעיקרו אלא מיגז גייז. וה"ה דמצי למימר דנפקא מינה אם שתתה ביין ונטמאה וגלחה במזיד, ואח"כ היפר לה — דאי מיעקר עקר אינה לוקה, ואי מיגז גייז לוקה. וכן לענין אם נטמאה בשוגג, ואח"כ היפר: אי מיעקר עקר — לא תביא עולת העוף ואשם; ואי מיגז גייז — מביאה עולת העוף ואשם, שהרי חל הנזירות עד עתה:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:4:1.english: If we say [the husband] uproots [the vow], her companion is also released - For it is as though the vow never took effect at all. And if we say he severs [it], she is released and her companion remains forbidden, because the first woman was subject to all the laws of naziriteship until the nullification, and the second woman properly associated [herself] with her; and the nullification of the first woman is of no benefit to the second. And granted that with regard to a sage, [if] the first vow was dissolved, they were all dissolved, that is because a sage uproots the vow from its inception, and it turns out as though it never took effect at all; but a husband, who nullifies without regret, does not uproot the vow from its inception, but rather severs [it]. And it could equally have said that the practical difference is [in a case where] she drank wine, became impure, or shaved intentionally, and afterward he nullified [the vow] for her: for if [he] uproots, she does not receive lashes, and if [he] severs, she receives lashes. And similarly regarding [the case where] she became impure unwittingly and afterward he nullified [the vow]: if [he] uproots, she does not bring a bird burnt-offering and a guilt-offering, and if [he] severs, she brings a bird burnt-offering and a guilt-offering, for the naziriteship was in effect until now.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:5:1.hebrew: אלא ש"מ בעל מיעקר עקר - ובהתרתה הוא מותר כמותה, דלא חל הנדר מעולם; ולכך אינו מיפר — דאינו מיפר לעצמו, אלא אחרים מוחלין לו. וצ"ע, דלא דמי לאחרים, דכיון דרשאי להפר לאשתו. ותירץ הר"ר אליהו דה"פ: אא"ב מיעקר עקר — אינו יכול להפר, דפשיטא דקיים לה, שאם לא קיים לה לא היה דיבורו שום דבר; אא"א מיגז גייז — א"כ אינו תלוי בדבורו, וכיון שאין תלוי בדבורו, ממילא הוי מופר:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:5:1.english: "Rather, conclude from this: A husband uproots" - And through the release of her [vow], he becomes permitted like her, for the vow never took effect [in the first place]. And for this reason he cannot nullify [her vow], as [a person] cannot nullify [a vow] for himself, but rather others [i.e., a court] release [it] for him. And this requires further study, for it is not comparable to other cases [of nullifying for oneself], since he is authorized to nullify for his wife [so his own release would merely be incidental]. And the Rabbi, Rabbi Eliyahu, resolved [this], explaining that this is the meaning: Granted if you say that [the husband] uproots [the vow retroactively], he cannot nullify [her vow], for it is obvious that he upheld [it] for her; since if he did not uphold [it] for her, his statement [of "and I"] would have been of no effect. But if you say that he severs [the vow from that point onward], if so, [the validity of his vow] does not depend on his statement [having upheld hers]; and since it does not depend on his statement, [her vow] is automatically nullified [when he nullifies it, while he remains bound].

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:6:1.hebrew: כמאן דאמר קיים ליכי דמי אי איתשיל אהקמתו מצי מיפר - [במאי] שאמר "קיים ליכי" — דאמת הוא דנשאלין על ההקמה, דהכי אמר רבי יוחנן בנדרים (דף סט.):
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:6:1.english: He is considered like one who said: "It is upheld for you; if he requests [dissolution] of his upholding, he can nullify" - [Regarding that] which [the Gemara] said, "It is upheld for you" — for it is indeed true that one may request [dissolution from a Sage] regarding an upholding, for so said Rabbi Yochanan in Nedarim (69a).

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:7:1.hebrew: האשה שנדרה בנזיר והפרישה בהמתה - חטאת, עולה, ושלמים. "אם שלו היתה הבהמה" - פי': מבהמות של בעלה. "תצא ותרעה בעדר" - כלומר: חולין היא, כיון שהיפר לה בעלה; וכדמפרש לקמן (נזיר דף כד.): דכי [מקנה] לה בעלה — מילתא דצריך לה, כלומר: אם לא היפר לה, שצריכה לקרבנות נזיר; במילתא דלא צריכה, כגון שהיפר לה בעלה ואינה צריכה לקרבנות נזיר — לא מקני לה:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:7:1.english: "A woman who vowed to be a nazirite and separated her animal" - [Namely,] a sin-offering, a burnt-offering, and peace-offerings. "If the animal was his" — explanation: from her husband's animals. "It shall go out and graze among the flock" — that is to say, it is non-sacred, since her husband nullified [the vow] for her; and as [the Gemara] explains below (Nazir 24a): That when her husband transfers ownership to her, [he transfers only] a matter that is needed by her — that is to say, if he did not nullify [her vow], so that she needs [it] for the offerings of a nazirite; [but] regarding a matter that is not needed [by her], such as where her husband nullified [her vow] and she does not need [it] for the offerings of a nazirite, he does not transfer ownership to her.

Tosafot on Nazir 21b:9:1.hebrew: והיינו טעמא דכיון דצריכה כפרה - על שציערה עצמה מן היין, וכרבי אלעזר הקפר דאמר: דנזיר חוטא הוא — הוה ליה חטאת (העוף) שמתו בעליה. אע"ג דהפר לה לענין [איסור], על הבהמה דין חטאת, אם הבהמה [שלה] היא, דגמרה ומקדיש לה:
Tosafot on Nazir 21b:9:1.english: "And this is the reason: Since she requires atonement" - [That is,] for having distressed herself [by abstaining] from wine, and in accordance with Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, who said that a nazirite is a sinner — [consequently,] it has the status of a sin-offering (of a bird) whose owners have died. Even though he nullified [the vow] for her regarding [the prohibition], upon the animal [applies] the status of a sin-offering if the animal was [hers], for she wholeheartedly consecrated it.
